description: 14a/14b — Verify the Chern-Simons κ derivation in prop:em-coupling-chern-simons at 100 dps. Computes det G^cl and det G^q from the paper's J²-jet Gram matrix on Bring's surface, with G_{ii} = CS_i + π²s_i²/c_i² and G_{12} = π²ℓ²/(c_1 c_2) for the force-carrier torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5}. Symbolic det G^cl = 605 π⁴ / 972. Numerical at q_0: κ = 1.72161454613... matches the paper's claim of 1.722. However, the κ that closes the α^{-1} residual to CODATA is 1.88777 (CODATA-2018) or 1.88805 (CODATA-2022). The 9.65% gap between the J² Gram-det κ and the CODATA-required κ is a real STRUCTURAL deficit, independent of CODATA version, suggesting a missing J³ or higher-order Gram correction.

vs_one_sixth.note: 1/6 is the closest simple closed form but not exact at 100 dps

verdict_14a: STRUCTURALLY_DERIVED — every ingredient (CS invariants, Gram entries, q-deformation) is a topological invariant of the torus knots T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}; no fitting.  Paper's κ = 1.722 reproduces from the formula at high precision.
verdict_14b: OPEN — closing the 398 ppb α residual requires a 9.65% increase in κ.  Three candidate sources for the missing 0.166: (a) J³ Gram correction (triple intersections on Bring's surface), (b) exceptional-divisor self-pairing beyond linear δ_CS, (c) missing π²-factor in Vol(S³_q)/Vol(S³_cl) normalisation.  The 1/6 closed-form candidate is intriguing but 0.31% off at 100 dps.

ppb_propagation_to_mH.verdict: α residual at 398 ppb propagates to ≈0.012 ppb on m(¹H).  Well below the m_p input σ floor of 0.3 ppb.  m(¹H) prediction is 1-ppb-class regardless of the κ gap.

next_steps: 14b-deeper: derive the J³ Gram correction algebraically.  Set up the 3-knot Gram with self+pair+triple intersections.
Check whether κ_req = 1/6 + Gram-det is exact at 200 dps (if not, rule out the 1/6 candidate).
If 14b stalls: declare ¹H closed at 0.4 ppb (input σ floor) and pivot to F.2 / Term 7 alternatives.
